scope:
Every milestone deserves an explanation.

TurnaroundSync is a proposed aviation operations and knowledge workbench. Our vision is that every turnaround milestone and exception has a source, a named dispatcher acknowledgment and an after-action explanation without changing safety-critical operations.

Our mission

Help authorized station teams notice and investigate missed handoffs earlier while respecting A-CDM procedures, local roles and dispatcher authority.

Where we are today

This is a research-stage website and isolated synthetic demonstration. No real customers, published operational integrations, paid trial, accepted pricing, demand or million-dollar revenue has been demonstrated.

A narrow starting point

Start with milestone reconciliation at one stand, with one airline, one handler and an airport rights owner. The operating user is a dispatcher. The buyer is an airline station director or contracted handler operations VP; airport operations/A-CDM owners review data rights and safety/security.

Five separate proposed offers

Ramp Desk reconciles milestones. Ramp Review evaluates uncertain risk advisories. Ramp Proof examines resource coverage conflicts. Ramp Signal reconstructs handoff and delay-code evidence. Ramp Report analyzes station process conformance. No module issues safety-critical commands.

The ambition is a carefully made, credible product experience. A premium design is not proof of commercial value, deployable-agent ROI or willingness to pay.
why:
Different records. Different questions.

Airline, handler and airport systems may record different times for the same handoff. A-CDM supports collaborative information exchange and pre-departure predictability. A discrepancy still needs a clear source, a reviewer and an explanation.

Coordination already exists

AODB systems, dispatch tools, radio and phone coordination and vendors such as Assaia are existing alternatives. Computer-vision event detection is not a blank space. The proposed opportunity is approved cross-party exception resolution and evidence capture.

The cost of another queue

False alerts, interruption, data rights, labor agreements, integration effort and airside safety may outweigh the value of another coordination tool. The trial must compare useful incremental evidence against the actual installed workflow and real dispatcher decisions.

One question to test first

Can a sourced milestone discrepancy help a dispatcher investigate a handoff without changing operations or increasing distraction? If real-time alerts distract, test after-action evidence instead.

demo:
Synthetic demonstration specification

Persistent badges on every frame: DEMO — SYNTHETIC DATA and CONCEPT PREVIEW. Charts and reports also carry ILLUSTRATIVE. Use fictional airport “Example Field”, airline “Example Air”, handler “Example Handling”, flight DEMO-050 and stand AV-07. N. Rao is a fictional dispatcher. Do not display IATA/ICAO identifiers that suggest a real airport.

1440×900 principal screen: 72px identity/status bar; 220px queue; central timeline with airline/handler/airport tracks; 320px evidence pane; review card and dated next action; report link. At 390px, stack record summary, tracks as labeled rows, evidence and review controls. Keep source labels and concept badges in view. No shrunken desktop canvas.

Storyboard

  1. Open the queue with 10 internally consistent synthetic records and derived status counts.
  2. Open AV07-CAT-01: a planned catering completion at 10:18 UTC has no matching completion assertion at the fixed replay time 10:22 UTC.
  3. Inspect source evidence. “No completion record received” is different from “catering did not complete.” Show missing information honestly.
  4. Switch to baggage discrepancy: handler says 10:16; airline says 10:19; both assertions remain visible. Do not average away the conflict.
  5. Inspect advisory: proposed next step is dispatcher review under existing procedures. N. Rao acknowledgment is pending; next review is 10:25 UTC, synthetic.
  6. Explicitly select a demo action: acknowledge for review, request more evidence, or reject advisory with reason. This changes only local fictional state. No external message or operational command.
  7. Open read-only after-action report with linked sources, uncertainty, reviewer note and draft delay-code reasoning. Pending records stay pending unless a deliberate action changed them.
  8. Include an honest failed recommendation: suggested coverage option rejected because authority/availability is unverified. Do not label any state “flight recovered.”

Document local event definitions, source ownership, event/observation time, timezone, correction rules and stale-data behavior. Local events and A-CDM context.

A-CDM establishes collaborative exchange and turnaround/pre-departure predictability. Local catering and baggage-completion observations are not automatically formal A-CDM milestones. Preserve local definitions and obtain the airport A-CDM owner's review before mapping a source assertion.

TimeMeaningExample in the synthetic record
PlannedA target in a fictional sourceCatering 10:18 UTC
EventWhat a source says happenedHandler baggage 10:16 UTC

research:
Evidence, assumptions and fieldwork.

Evidence is high for the operational standard and incumbent. Evidence is low for deployable-agent ROI. No interviews, purchase orders, paid LOIs or willingness-to-pay experiments were supplied or conducted.

1. Buyer proof

Interview each stakeholder separately, then qualify one shared-data triad. Confirm the budget owner, scope, authority, willingness to sponsor and dispatcher capacity. Acquisition hypotheses include handler enterprise accounts, airline station networks, airport innovation/procurement teams and A-CDM partners.

2. Bottom-up market proof

Segment only after validating payer, contract scope, penetration, retention and expansion. Model authorized stands × contracting stations, including integration overhead. Airport movements and societal delay costs are not addressable software spend. No unicorn or million-dollar outcome is established.

3. Competition

Named incumbents are adjacent examples, not an exhaustive current feature/pricing matrix. Live product trials and loss interviews remain required. The broader cross-concept research names FreightClaims, Clio, Loop and OpenGov as well as Assaia; the former examples are not aviation competitors.

4. Rights, privacy and regulation

Obtain written permissions and jurisdiction-specific counsel where appropriate. Do not ingest real claims, tenant, legal-client, benefit-applicant, research-subject or airside records into public demonstrations. Validate airside rights, AODB/A-CDM interfaces, sensor/video permission, aviation security, labor agreements and the safety case.

5. Task outcomes

Preregister baseline, comparator, unit of analysis, human override and adverse-outcome metrics. Model accuracy alone is insufficient. Include false-alert cost, review burden and whether the station controls a proposed action.

6. Source boundaries

Official standards establish workflow. Vendor pages establish what vendors say they sell. Neither proves customers will pay for a new provider. Recheck effective dates and product scope before implementation.

Expansion hypothesis

Additional authorized stands, stations and performance modules may follow measured handling reliability and credible attributable delay outcomes. Long procurement, separate budgets and multi-party integration constrain initial expansion.

Stakeholder outreach sequence — draft only, not sent

  1. Station lead: share a short A-CDM-context timestamp-conflict explainer. Ask how discrepancies are handled today and who owns the budget.
  2. Handler operations VP: share the synthetic handoff evidence example. Ask about dispatcher burden, coverage authority and a possible sponsor.
  3. Airport innovation/A-CDM owner: share the advisory boundary and rights checklist. Ask who can evaluate access/security/safety feasibility.
  4. Triad meeting: align one stand, one scenario, named decision owner and baseline/comparator; discuss the hypothetical four-week $5,000 sponsorship.
  5. Written commitment: seek rights, safety sign-off and paid sponsorship before real observation. Record denial, objections and loss reasons as evidence.

Ad test: small, pre-approved targeted LinkedIn outreach; compare “cross-party timestamp conflict” against “after-action evidence.” No safety-performance promise, novelty claim about computer vision, or guaranteed delay reduction. Measure qualified triad sponsorship conversations. Do not launch campaigns or send messages from this blueprint.

Future Notion fields: station/stand; airline/handler/airport sponsors; A-CDM/AODB sources; rights status; safety review; events sampled; false-alert count; dispatcher burden; attributable delay; trial fee; decision. Opportunity stages: Triad sponsor → Data rights → Safety review → Paid shadow trial.Decision gate

Advance only with permissions, a paid sponsor and safe shadow evidence above the incumbent workflow. Pivot to after-action evidence if alerts distract. Stop on data denial or adverse safety assessment.
